still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 37.2% ever-used − 24.8% current = 12.4% of adults who used and are off now. About 54% of current users are on a second or later course (13.4 points), and 3.4 points cycled and are off again, so (13.4 + 3.4) / 37.2 ≈ 45.2% of ever-users have cycled. The other ~9.0 points stopped once and have not restarted. Planned 'drug holidays' of under 8 weeks are not counted as stops. About 30% of maintenance users report at least one a year, so the cycling figure understates how often people interrupt. One-year persistence is still near one-third on cash weekly and oral products and ~60% inside conditioned tracks. Restart within a year is ~40%. Ever-use rose 2.6 points, about 7M new adult starters over two years, mostly on oral amycretin after its January 2036 TrumpRx listing and from 2035 employer-coverage losers who restarted on cash. Current use is flat because those inflows roughly equal the people who stopped when their coverage ended. Age check: 0.20×15 + 0.33×24.5 + 0.24×36 + 0.23×22 = 3.0 + 8.09 + 8.64 + 5.06 ≈ 24.8. Income thirds average 24.8. Users: 24.8% of ~276M adults ≈ 68.4M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~13.6M (down from 16.5M; ~5.7M on diabetes/CV/CKD/OSA codes, ~7.9M in conditioned weight tracks); Medicare ~15.2M; Medicaid ~5.0M (~1.1M on the AUD label); legitimate cash ~29.4M (incl. ~6.6M indefinite $149 starting-dose users and ~2.1M calm/focus subscribers); imported or counterfeit ~5.2M. Sum: 13.6 + 15.2 + 5.0 + 29.4 + 5.2 = 68.4. The middle third fell 0.5 points because 2035 employer retreats hit mid-wage salaried workers hardest, and about 0.9M of those who lost coverage did not move to cash. The bottom third rose 0.5 points on Medicaid AUD growth and cheaper cash brands. Off-drug populations: ~34M adults are former users. ~20% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and adults 65+ without qualifying codes. Pediatric: ~3.2% of 12–17s and ~0.6% of 6–11s, with ~60% of 6–11 starts Medicaid/CHIP under EPSDT. About 5.8M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~15.2M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) and AUD codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 15.2M × ~$214 average net/month × 12 ≈ $39.0B gross Part D incretin spend. Users rose ~1.2M while average net fell ~6% from $228 under negotiated-price and rebate pressure, so total spend is nearly flat (from ~$38.3B). CMS's AUD coding audit (closed Oct 2035) found ~14% of sampled telehealth-originated AUD diagnoses unsupported. Recoupments were sought from three platforms; nothing changed for beneficiaries. Medicaid (~5.0M): 5.0M × ~$165 net × 12 ≈ $9.9B. AUD remains a covered outpatient drug in every state. 7 states still cover adult weight-loss use, and 4 of them (up from 2) now condition renewal on verified adherence and BMI progress. Children 6–11 are still reached through EPSDT.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month inside India and in 100+ export markets, and Indian exporters have grown in the Gulf, Latin America and Africa. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials still sell for $20–60 where patents are not enforced. Under the Section 232 tariff and export-licence regime, which is still in force, delivered US prices are ~$90–170. Canadian and Brazilian generics cost CAD 40–75 and BRL 150–260.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Business Group on Health (Nov 2035): 26% of employers cover weight-management use, down from 33%. ~80% of those condition coverage on verified adherence and/or ≥5% loss at six months, and unconditional coverage is ~5%. Nearly all employers still cover incretins under diabetes, CV, CKD and OSA codes, so access now splits by diagnosis code, not by drug. About 1 in 5 employers that dropped weight coverage replaced it with a $50–100/month HSA or wellness stipend pointed at TrumpRx, a defined-contribution model brokers call 'point-to-cash'. Managed decline through negotiated channels: TrumpRx Wegovy pill starting dose $149, maintenance $179 (from $199). Foundayo $149–199. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $199–249 (from $249–299). MariTide $229 direct. Oral amycretin was added to TrumpRx in Jan 2036 at $299 (from ~$449 cash direct) and has ~6.0M users. Retatrutide ~$329 cash. Orals are ~64% of users. Gray market ~5.2M (7.6% of users). Falling brand prices narrowed the gap to $90–170 gray vials, but domestic re-filling of smuggled API persists in the Deep South, where the price still matters.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide). The 60+ without CVD extension received a complete response letter in Feb 2036
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' low-dose plans via telehealth (~2.1M subscribers, down from 2.4M), still partly routed onto the AUD label
planned 'drug holidays' and self-directed dose-downs, especially 'Foundayo weekends' that exploit orforglipron's short half-life
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid
indefinite use of the $149 TrumpRx starting dose (~6.6M people)
semaglutide in 12–14-year-olds above label titration in gray channels
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new indication was approved this step. Lilly resubmitted the tirzepatide dementia extension for adults 60+ without CVD in Apr 2035. FDA issued a complete response letter in Feb 2036 asking for fracture-mitigation data in women 70+. The oral_parity driver is realised through an existing product, as the rules allow: Novo's head-to-head trial of oral amycretin against weekly tirzepatide (read out Jun 2035) met non-inferiority at 72 weeks (−21.2% vs −20.6%). Oral amycretin then joined TrumpRx at $299 in Jan 2036 and most commercial formularies at parity with injectables, which removed the needle as a reason to choose injectables for that efficacy tier. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%. No new oral incretin has been filed with a stated phase 3 programme, so none can reach market this window. Implants remain in phase 1–2. Global incretin market ~$200B (2035). Ex-US volume grew while US net prices fell ~5–8% a year through TrumpRx, Medicare negotiation and PBM deals.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside tracks. Drug holidays have produced a wave of re-titration nausea when people restart at full dose without stepping back up.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; restart-titration language added to semaglutide and tirzepatide labels (2035).

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first two MDL bellwethers (2035) split, one defense verdict and one $4.1M plaintiff verdict on causation for a patient who did not titrate. Claims passed ~44,000. Whether gastroparesis persists after stopping is still disputed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling; more bellwethers set for 2036–37.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The fracture excess in women 70+ in the dementia trial was the basis of the Feb 2036 CRL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code in use; bimagrumab restricted label unchanged (~210k users).

safety_ledger.effect: NAION (non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy) and related optic-nerve events
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A Sentinel distributed analysis of ~22M users, pooled with RCT adjudication across semaglutide, tirzepatide and amycretin programmes, found HR ~1.9 (95% CI 1.6–2.3) for NAION. The excess is ~1 per 10,000 person-years, highest in users over 50 with diabetes, sleep apnea or a small crowded optic disc. That is roughly 4,000–6,000 attributable cases a year across ~68M users. Most affected eyes do not recover lost vision. There is no clear difference between molecules, and data are insufficient for retatrutide and MariTide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class warning (Sep 2035) on all GLP-1-receptor-agonist-containing products: stop promptly with sudden painless vision loss, counsel patients with prior NAION in one eye, and consider a baseline eye exam in high-risk patients. Medication guides updated. FMCSA and FAA added an examiner question. A NAION arm opened in the MDL (~6,500 claims).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal through three years of AUD-label use.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA observational figures (~7% at maintenance vs ~3.5% controls; ~10% on retatrutide) are unchanged. A Novo-funded low-dose substudy began enrolling calm-dose users in 2035 and has no readout. Surveys suggest most planned drug holidays are taken for blunting rather than GI reasons.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. ACP/OMA guidance (Apr 2036) recognises dose reduction and planned interruptions as reasonable responses to blunting.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. The 2035 employer retreat added ~0.9M stoppers who did not move to cash, mostly mid-wage salaried workers. Short holidays produce modest, mostly recovered regain of 1–3%.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; still the actuarial basis for conditioned coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine (AUD users who keep drinking); low ferritin in adolescent girls.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual panel language on labels; thiamine counselling on the AUD label.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims ~61,000. The DOJ civil investigative demand into Novo is still open.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled for semaglutide and tirzepatide; FDA reviewing Novo's full extension dataset; no new action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up. Cycling and holiday effects on bone, pancreas and the optic nerve are poorly characterised. Still no data on indefinite starting-dose use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Non-approved-product adverse-event reports passed ~36,000. A second CDC cluster (2035) traced ~90 infections to re-filled vials in Alabama and Georgia, with 1 death. Poison-centre calls are at ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Section 232 tariff and Indian export checks unchanged. No federal statute; Mississippi made unlicensed peptide re-filling a felony (2035).

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The STEP Young extension at 2.5 years shows a persistent ~0.5 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters and partial catch-up in those who stopped. The Swedish registry ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language and medication guide; no REMS; AAP still prefers lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~1 per 2,000 person-years, concentrated in titration and in restarts after holidays.

safety_ledger.effect: Re-titration intolerance after planned drug holidays
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ED networks report severe vomiting and dehydration in users who resume a maintenance dose after 3+ weeks off. Estimated ~1 ED visit per 1,500 holidays on weekly injectables and long-half-life orals.

food_and_beverage.state: About 42% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~14–15% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~12%. With adoption flat, per-capita declines slowed to under 1% a year, and the shift to higher-efficacy orals deepens per-user effects only modestly. The industry now plans for a stable 'quarter-on' market. Weekend snack sales tick up measurably in suburbs where Foundayo weekends are common, and retailers in Columbus and Indianapolis now schedule Saturday promotions around it.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~19% from 2025 and beer ~12%. AUD-label Medicaid and EAP use keeps eroding heavy drinkers. Bardstown-area distilleries cut a further ~900 jobs, and Brown-Forman-style producers lean on exports. Holiday-weekend drinking spikes are a recognised pattern that distributors stock for.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Portion tiers are standard. Late-night bar revenue in Dayton, Toledo and Louisville has stabilised at a lower level. Some casual chains run 'off-week' promotions.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialty keeps shrinking. Mass retailers serving the 2035 coverage losers see size-up returns. Stretch, resale and tailoring keep growing.

fitness.state: Strength training is still growing. Conditioned tracks still require InBody scans. The employer-to-cash shift cut corporate gym subsidies, so budget chains gain and boutique coaching tied to employer tracks slows.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage fell to 26%, while diabetes and cardiac code coverage stayed near-universal, so plans have hardened their PA reviews for those codes. Point-to-cash stipends are spreading. Pharmacy trend fell to ~+4% as weight claims left. Adherence premium differentials are standard among the employers that still cover. Part D premiums rose modestly.

pharma.state: US unit volume is flat and US net prices fell, so US revenue is roughly flat, and growth comes from ex-US. Novo rides oral amycretin's TrumpRx listing while carrying the litigation reserve and the open DOJ demand. Lilly lost the dementia extension for now and absorbed the NAION class warning, which hit all players equally. Amgen's MariTide is still strong inside tracks. Litigation-finance firms recruit NAION plaintiffs.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being slim-on-drug is no longer a signal. It is the default for the insured and cash-paying middle aged. What reads now is the gap. Visible regain in a 45-year-old in Columbus says 'your employer dropped it in 2035'. A Saturday dessert says 'Foundayo weekend'. A sudden plateau of softness says 'holiday'. In the Delta, regain still reads as the hunger tax.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle is still the upper-tier uniform, and 'off-drug lean' is still the elite boast, but it now needs a story: genetics, a trainer, a pregnancy. The two tiers are covered-by-code (diabetes, CV, Medicare) and cash-by-choice at $149–299, with stipends bridging some of the middle. Upper-income parents still mostly refuse prepubertal semaglutide.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Weekday meals are small and quick. Weekends have become the eating days for people on short-half-life pills, and Saturday brunch rebounded in Columbus and Indianapolis suburbs. Office birthday cakes are mostly symbolic, and the person who eats a full slice is asked, kindly, whether they are 'off right now'. Bread Alone's full-table suppers persist but the movement has stopped growing.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Major apps dropped the 'calm plan' tag in 2035 because most users picked it. The newer profile field is 'off (by choice)', which signals either health anxiety or an appetite for wine and late dinners. The AUD tag remains. Couples schedule shared holidays, a week off together before a trip or an anniversary.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is now something you schedule. On-drug is unremarkable, and off-drug needs a reason: pregnancy, the eye warning, a holiday, a lost plan. 'Let Them Grow' has narrowed to a pediatric-policy group. Unmuted's new slogan is 'the right to feel', aimed at adherence tracks rather than at the drug. Fat-acceptance groups have shrunk.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Measured anhedonia is unchanged at ~7% of maintenance users vs ~3.5% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. What changed is the conversation. About 30% of maintenance users report at least one planned holiday a year, and ~1 in 6 have self-directed a dose-down. 'Flat' is ordinary vocabulary, as in 'I'm a bit flat this month'. Calm-plan subscriptions fell from 2.4M to 2.1M as the feature became a complaint. Low-dose anhedonia is still unmeasured.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect you manage, like statin aches. Clinicians call it dose-related blunting and now have guidance for it. Platforms rebranded from 'quiet the noise' to 'tune your dose'. HR calls holidays a 'documented dose adjustment'. Unmuted calls conditioned adherence 'mandatory flatness'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 7.9M workers are still in conditioned tracks, and there holidays are an adherence breach unless a clinician files the new holiday code. The three largest track vendors allow up to 6 weeks a year without penalty to the premium tier. Smart-bottle logs flag undeclared gaps. Several Teamsters and SEIU locals bargained holiday clauses into 2036 contracts. Since the NAION warning, FMCSA and FAA medical examiners ask about vision changes on incretins. The two EEOC charges are still unresolved.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday' became a genre. Comedians and novelists write the week someone comes off and feels everything at once. Festival promoters in Louisville and Columbus book around long weekends because ticket buyers time holidays to them. Sportsbooks see a small holiday-weekend handle spike.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists now ask about dose schedules as routinely as about work schedules. Shared holidays are a courtship and anniversary ritual. A familiar complaint is the partner who is 'better company off' but less steady.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: With normalisation, the drug itself is no longer much of a partisan marker. The live fight is over conditioning: state employee plans that log adherence, the holiday codes, and Illinois's ban, which no other state has copied. A California ban bill died in committee in 2035. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA remains routine. It issued the NAION class warning, a CRL on the dementia extension, restart-titration labelling and more untitled letters to calm platforms. CMS closed its AUD coding audit with platform recoupments. States moved, but toward conditioning rather than restriction.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new subsidy. By plan year 2036, 14 state employee health plans (including Texas ERS, Georgia SHBP, Indiana and Florida) cover weight-management incretins only with verified adherence and ≥5% loss at six months, and 4 of the 7 Medicaid programmes covering weight use condition renewal. OPM's FEHB conditions continue. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Adherence feeds from smart bottles, PBM fills and clinic logs now flow to state employee plans as well as to FEHB carriers and large employers. Holiday codes are a new data field, so a planned interruption is recorded too. After the warning, some track vendors added vision-symptom questions to monthly check-ins. Illinois remains the only ban.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE still covers the AUD label, and the Army recruit oral pilot continues. FMCSA and FAA added vision questions after the NAION warning, and FMCSA guidance is still silent on calm plans.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 100% tariff and India's export-licence checks remain. A WTO panel on Beijing's complaint was established in 2035 and has not ruled. Smuggled API still feeds domestic re-filling in the Deep South. Branded US and Danish plants are exempt and supply the TrumpRx channel.

events.event: Plan year 2035 opens with a wave of large employers dropping weight-management coverage while keeping diabetes and cardiac codes; Business Group on Health's November survey puts weight coverage at 26% of employers, down from 33%, and about 1 in 5 dropping employers now pay a TrumpRx-directed stipend instead
Novo's head-to-head trial finds daily oral amycretin non-inferior to weekly tirzepatide at 72 weeks (−21.2% vs −20.6%); commercial formularies move the pill to parity with injectables

Texas, Georgia, Indiana, Florida and ten other states adopt adherence-and-progress conditions for weight-drug coverage in their employee health plans for 2036; two more Medicaid programmes condition renewal on logged adherence

FDA adds a class warning for NAION to every GLP-1-receptor-agonist product after a Sentinel analysis finds roughly doubled risk, about one excess case per 10,000 person-years; FMCSA and FAA add vision questions for examiners
TrumpRx lists oral amycretin at $299 a month, down from about $449 cash, and cuts Wegovy pill maintenance to $179; Medicare negotiation and PBM deals take branded injectables to $199–249 cash

ACP and the Obesity Medicine Association issue guidance endorsing dose reductions and planned interruptions for patients reporting blunting; the three largest adherence-track vendors add a clinician-filed 'dose holiday' code allowing up to six weeks a year without premium penalty

open_tensions: Drug holidays are now clinically endorsed and culturally ordinary, but 7.9M track members and state employees can take them only through a logged clinician code. Undeclared gaps still cost premium tiers, and the holiday code is itself a new surveillance field.

The employer retreat pushed weight-only users into a cash tier at $149–299 with no routine clinician contact, just as the NAION class warning asks for baseline eye exams in high-risk users and the 6.6M indefinite starting-dose users remain unstudied.
Medicaid children 6–11 on semaglutide still grow ~0.5 cm a year slower, upper-income parents still opt out, and final adult height is years away.

Lilly's dementia extension was refused on hip-fracture data, but cash dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds continues. Medicare spend (~$39B) is flat only because falling prices offset rising users.

prose.headline: Nobody Asks If You're On It Anymore. They Ask Why You Stopped.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about one American adult in four takes an incretin drug, the same share as two years ago. The stillness on the chart is made of motion. About seven million people started for the first time, mostly on a pill. About as many stopped, many because their employer stopped paying. The total stayed near sixty-eight million.

The pill is the story people tell. In June 2035 Novo showed that daily oral amycretin takes off as much weight as weekly tirzepatide. In January the TrumpRx channel listed it at $299 a month. Nearly two-thirds of users now swallow rather than inject. The needle no longer decides anything, and the money still does. Brand prices kept slipping through negotiated channels: the Wegovy maintenance pill is $179, the injectables are $199 to $249, and the $149 starting pill is still what six and a half million people stay on indefinitely. Nothing is cheap. Everything is a little cheaper.

The employers made the other story. In the 2035 benefit season large companies dropped weight-management coverage in numbers, keeping it only for diabetes and heart codes, and the share of employers covering weight use fell from a third to about a quarter. Some replaced it with a monthly stipend pointed at TrumpRx, and brokers call this point-to-cash. A system has hardened in which your diagnosis code, not your drug, decides whether an insurer or you pay. Mid-wage salaried workers lost the most. In the suburbs of Columbus and Indianapolis the regain of 2035 looks different from Memphis's tariff regain two years earlier, slower and better dressed, but it is the same arithmetic.

Where coverage survived, it comes with conditions. The federal employee programme already required proof of adherence. In 2035 fourteen state employee plans, Texas, Georgia, Indiana and Florida among them, followed. Four of the seven state Medicaid programmes that pay for weight use now renew coverage only for members whose logs stay full. Illinois's ban on adherence-tied premiums is still the only one; California's version died in committee.

In September 2035 the FDA put a warning on every drug in the class: sudden, painless loss of vision in one eye, an optic-nerve stroke called NAION, about twice as likely on the drugs. The absolute risk is small, roughly one extra case per ten thousand users a year. Across sixty-eight million people that is several thousand eyes a year, most of which do not recover. Truck-driver and pilot examiners now ask about it. Lawyers opened a new arm of the litigation. Very few people stopped.

That is the clearest sign of where the culture has gone. Taking the drug no longer marks you. Not taking it does. At an office lunch in Grove City the person who eats a full slice of cake is asked, gently, whether they are off right now, and the accepted answers are a pregnancy, a lost plan, the eye thing, or a holiday.

The holiday is the habit of these two years. The calm platforms spent 2034 selling the flattened feeling as a feature. By 2036 it is a complaint people make the way they once complained about statin aches. 'I'm a bit flat' is ordinary speech. Nearly a third of long-term users plan a break each year. Foundayo, which clears the body in a day or two, made Saturday skips a suburban ritual, and grocers in Ohio now run weekend promotions around it. In April the physicians' societies endorsed planned interruptions. The track vendors answered with a holiday code a clinician can file to protect your premium tier for up to six weeks. Undeclared gaps still show up on the smart bottle. Feeling things now needs paperwork.

The children's question is unanswered. Medicaid six-to-eleven-year-olds still grow half a centimetre a year more slowly on semaglutide, and their adult height is years away.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renée Kowalski skips her Saturday pill on purpose. The orange Foundayo bottle stays shut on the windowsill, and its cap light blinks once, a sound she no longer hears. Nobody logs her. Her company dropped weight coverage in January 2035, and now she pays TrumpRx $179 a month out of a $75 stipend and her own checking account.

Mark's bottle is different. His plan through the state pays for Zepbound only if the log stays full, so his pen goes in Sunday night and the app turns green. Last spring he filed a holiday code for their anniversary. His nurse practitioner typed it in while asking about his sex life and his eyes in the same tone.

By ten Renée is hungry the way she remembers. At the Kroger on Stringtown Road the end caps say WEEKEND, with cinnamon rolls, chips and real cream. She buys the rolls.

Her sister Dee calls from Toledo to say she's off for good. The eye warning scared her, and she has a crowded disc, whatever that means. Renée asks how she'll explain it at work. Dee says she'll say she's trying for a baby, at forty-one. They both laugh.

At her nephew's birthday the cake is mostly decoration. A cousin eats two pieces, and someone asks if he's on a holiday. He says no, he's just off, and the yard goes quiet.

That night Renée cries at a dog-food commercial, laughs at herself, and pours a second glass of wine. Tomorrow at seven she'll swallow the pill again and be steady by Tuesday.

least_plausible_claims.quote: mostly on oral amycretin after its January 2036 TrumpRx listing and from 2035 employer-coverage losers who restarted on cash
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: people who lost coverage and 'restarted' on cash are already ever-users, so they cannot raise ever-use. The 2.6-point rise therefore rests on first-time starters alone, and the claimed driver is only partly valid.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Major apps dropped the 'calm plan' tag in 2035 because most users picked it.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world's own figures put calm/focus subscribers at ~2.1M, about 3% of 68M users, and falling from 2.4M. 'Most users picked it' contradicts that and gives no reason for the tag to vanish.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Weekend snack sales tick up measurably in suburbs where Foundayo weekends are common, and retailers in Columbus and Indianapolis now schedule Saturday promotions around it.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: a habit of skipping single doses of one orforglipron product, one of ~12 incretin classes and not the dominant oral, is asserted to move local retail sales. Skipping a dose of a drug that clears in a day or two would blunt appetite suppression only slightly, and the effect is too specific and fast for the evidence given.
